question.problem:
Find the radius of convergence $R$ for the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(x-2)^{n}}{n!}=(x-2)+\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{2!}+\frac{(x-2)^{3}}{3!}+⋯\,.
$$

$R=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{(x-2)^{n}}{n!}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{\frac{(x-2)^{n+1}}{(n+1)!}}{\frac{(x-2)^{n}}{n!}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(x-2)^{n+1}}{(n+1)!}\cdot \frac{n!}{(x-2)^{n}}| \\  & =|x-2|{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{1}{n+1} \\  & =|x-2|\cdot 0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied for all $-\infty <x<\infty .$  Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=\infty .$
